title: Sort an Array: Bubble Sort to Merge Sort
contract: Return integers sorted in ascending order, retaining duplicates.
brute: for(int end=a.length-1;end>0;end--){boolean changed=false;for(int i=0;i<end;i++)if(a[i]>a[i+1]){int t=a[i];a[i]=a[i+1];a[i+1]=t;changed=true;emit("Swap an inverted adjacent pair","array",a,"indices",new int[]{i,i+1});}if(!changed)break;}return a;
optimal: int n=a.length;int[] temp=new int[n];for(int width=1;width<n;width*=2){for(int l=0;l<n;l+=2*width){int mid=Math.min(l+width,n),r=Math.min(l+2*width,n),i=l,j=mid,k=l;while(i<mid||j<r)temp[k++]=(j>=r||(i<mid&&a[i]<=a[j]))?a[i++]:a[j++];for(k=l;k<r;k++)a[k]=temp[k];emit("Merge two sorted runs","array",a,"bounds",new int[]{l,mid,r});}if(width>n/2)break;}return a;
reasoning: Bubble sort removes adjacent inversions; the largest remaining value reaches the end after each pass.
Merge sort begins with sorted singleton runs and repeatedly merges neighboring runs.
During merge, take the smallest available head; choosing the left on equality preserves stability. Each pass is linear and there are logarithmically many passes.
complexity: O(n log n), O(n); comparison-model worst-case optimal
